title: Restore
intro: Bring back a downloaded backup. This replaces the whole database; nexcrate makes a copy of the current state first.
passwordHint: The password you chose when downloading.
tooNew: This backup comes from version {{version}} and is newer than the running nexcrate. Update nexcrate first, then restore.
unknownVersion: This backup does not say which version it comes from, so it cannot be restored.
outside: nexcrate only brings itself back. What happened since in the download clients, on the disk or in Radarr, Sonarr and Lidarr stays as it is; nexcrate catches up with it bit by bit afterwards.
keyOnlyFromEnv: The archive holds no key. This installation takes its key from NEXCRATE_SECRET_KEY: the stored credentials are only readable afterwards if it holds the same value as when the backup was made.
noKeyAtAll: The archive holds no key, and this installation has none in NEXCRATE_SECRET_KEY. After restoring, no stored credential is readable (TMDB, indexers, download clients, connections); you would have to enter them all again.
envKeyWarning: This installation takes its key from NEXCRATE_SECRET_KEY. That value wins over the key in the archive: if it differs, the stored credentials are unreadable afterwards.
replaceWarning: Everything that happened in nexcrate since this backup is lost. nexcrate restarts for it and is unreachable for a few minutes; afterwards nobody is logged in.
restarting: nexcrate restarts and restores the backup. With a large database this takes a few minutes; the page reloads by itself afterwards.
gaveUp: nexcrate has not answered for 45 minutes. Look at the log of the container to see what happens at the start.
setupIntro: Had nexcrate before? Restore a downloaded backup instead of starting empty. The account comes from the backup; log in with it afterwards.
freshNote: nexcrate restarts for it and is unreachable for a moment. Afterwards you log in with the account from the backup.
